CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to reassess the management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, expressing a mixed but generally positive response to the ongoing treatment regimen. He reports that the frequency of his tension-type headaches has remained stable at approximately 2 times per week, with the intensity slightly reduced to an average score of 3 out of 10. He attributes this improvement to the consistent use of topiramate and the ongoing efficacy of amitriptyline, which he has been taking nightly.
Sleep quality has further improved; Mr. Smith now averages about 7 hours of sleep per night, with fewer awakenings. He reports that trazodone and melatonin have been effective, but he still experiences occasional difficulties in initiating sleep, particularly on nights when work-related stressors are heightened. He is interested in discussing alternative medications or adjunct therapies to enhance sleep onset.
Fatigue persists, particularly in the mornings, but Mr. Smith notes that engaging in regular exercise, including running and yoga, has contributed positively to his overall energy levels throughout the day. He continues to experience mild fatigue but denies any new symptoms such as dizziness or lethargy.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 250 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime (continued) 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 6. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 7. Topiramate 100 mg daily (continued) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, where he has implemented better time management strategies to mitigate stress. He remains physically active, participating in running and yoga, which he believes significantly enhance his mood and energy. He maintains a balanced diet, abstains from alcohol, and keeps his caffeine consumption low.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels stable; some improvement in sleep quality; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency stable; no dizziness or visual disturbances reported. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent mild fatigue noted, with no fever or weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented, appears well-groomed; mood appears stable with mild anxiety noted. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no dizziness reported. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with no signs of distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 250 mg daily. Monitor for any changes in anxiety levels. Lorazepam usage remains as needed for acute episodes. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone and melatonin; consider adding a low-dose gabapentin at bedtime to assist with sleep onset if difficulties persist. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 100 mg daily; monitor headache frequency and intensity. Continue amitriptyline at 50 mg nightly. Schedule a follow-up in one month to assess response to the current regimen. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Reinforce the importance of regular physical activity and mindfulness practices. If fatigue persists or worsens, consider further evaluation for underlying causes.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-06-01 to monitor symptom changes, evaluate treatment efficacy, and discuss any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to maintain a headache diary and track sleep patterns to identify potential triggers and improve management strategies.
